definition: The recorded outcome of a contested citation after a hearing — upheld, reduced, or dismissed — which advances the citation-lifecycle to its adjudicated state.
name: adjudication

definition: A context-aware chat that answers grounded in the current screen, role, and row, respecting permissions and redaction, with per-turn cost telemetry.
name: portal-assistant

definition: A numbered TT-* record stating a precise platform rule, linked from the features, transitions, and tests that implement and verify it.
name: business-rule

definition: A traffic ticket: one driver, one violation type, one issuing jurisdiction, an issue date, and the case hub from which all four status tracks are derived.
name: citation

definition: The top-level computed track: Issued → Responded → InContest → Adjudicated → Closed.
name: citation-status

definition: The terminal payment state reached when a citation remains unpaid beyond the jurisdiction's DaysLateToCollections window.
name: collections

definition: A recognized legal basis for disputing a citation (signage, malfunction, emergency, calibration, mistaken identity), drawn from the ContestGrounds catalog per ViolationType.
name: contest-ground

definition: The hearing track: NotContested | HearingRequested → Scheduled → Heard.
name: contest-status

definition: Per-turn records of assistant/OCR token usage and dollar cost, rolled up by model, role, and case for the cost dashboard.
name: cost-telemetry

definition: A per-jurisdiction window (contest, payment, appeal) in DeadlineRules that determines a citation's computed deadlines and late penalties.
name: deadline-rule

definition: What happens when a citation's response window passes with no response — it is adjudicated against the driver automatically.
name: default-judgment

definition: The formal ruling on a contest, captured on the Citation and rendered into a determination letter from the jurisdiction template.
name: determination

definition: The official outcome document generated from a hearing determination using the jurisdiction's template.
name: determination-letter

definition: The cited party — the person who received the traffic citation and whose license points roll up across their citations.
name: driver

definition: The public self-service surface where a driver looks up their own citation and chooses to pay or contest.
name: driver-portal

definition: The visual inference graph showing how a calculated field (e.g. a contest deadline) is derived from raw inputs and lookups.
name: explainer-dag

definition: The per-(jurisdiction, violation) base fine and surcharge percentage in FeeSchedules that drives a citation's amount due.
name: fee-schedule

definition: The base monetary penalty for a violation, taken from the violation type's BaseFineUsd.
name: fine

definition: A contest event: requested by the driver, scheduled by a manager, and concluded with an outcome (e.g. Dismissed) that drives liability.
name: hearing

definition: The regulatory authority (county or city) that issued a citation. Its row holds every deadline, fine, penalty, and point threshold that governs cases under it.
name: jurisdiction

definition: A per-state law governing fines, surcharges, deadlines, and point schedules, sourced from JurisdictionRules.
name: jurisdiction-rule

definition: An additional charge of LatePenaltyPct of the fine, applied when payment misses the pay-by date.
name: late-penalty

definition: The driver track: Valid → Warning → Suspended, driven by active points against jurisdiction thresholds.
name: license-status

definition: Per-package/feature/table/route entitlement toggles that add or remove surfaces from the platform without code changes.
name: licensing

definition: A supervisor who schedules hearings and reviews/approves submissions.
name: manager

definition: The money track: Pending → Due → Late → Collections | Paid | NotOwed.
name: payment-status

definition: Demerit points attached to a violation type; they accumulate on the driver and can trigger a license warning or suspension.
name: points

definition: Role-Based Access Control: the role->table->field CRUD model plus WHERE policies and redaction that govern who can do what.
name: rbac

definition: Masking of PII fields (license number, address) for roles like external-llm at the moment a row leaves the database.
name: redaction

definition: A line agent who owns cases and completes domain workflows on behalf of, or alongside, the driver.
name: representative

definition: Derived Postgres predicates that scope each role's visible rows (e.g. a representative sees only assigned citations), compiled from WHERE policies.
name: row-level-security

definition: The pattern of expressing regulations as data on the Jurisdictions table, so changing a value re-derives every dependent citation with no code change.
name: rules-engine

definition: A data-defined lifecycle (citation-lifecycle, contest-track, payment-track, license-track) of states and guarded transitions enforced by the backbone.
name: state-machine

definition: A percentage added to the base fine per jurisdiction, contributing to the total amount due on a citation.
name: surcharge

definition: The condition (referencing a business rule) that must hold for a state transition to fire, plus the role allowed to fire it.
name: transition-guard

definition: The prioritized list of non-terminal items (deadlines, hearings, payments) a role must act on, scoped by that role's WHERE policy.
name: work-queue
